catalog_locator: Section 2.2.3 'Tonemes', pp. 104-111 (Table 8, Figs. 1-4, tone sandhi P Rules 2-3); archive.org djvu text layer
catalog_quote: 2.2.3 Tonemes. The primary supra-segmental features are the six tones given in Table 8. ... [Table 8: 1 yin-p'ing sheng ... mid level legato tone; 2 yang-p'ing sheng ... low level (a little falling) legato tone; 3 shang sheng ... mid falling legato tone; 4 ch'u sheng ... high level (a little rising) legato tone; 5 yin-ju sheng ... mid falling staccato tone; 6 yang-ju sheng ... high rising staccato tone] ... The pitch and stress of these six tones as pronounced in individual utterances are shown in Figure 1. These were produced by recording the speech of the informant through the "Pitch-Stress Recorder." ... Figures 2, 3, and 4 show the pitch- and stress-gram of the six tones in all the dissyllabic combinations possible in Moi-yan. ... Tone sandhi in Moi-yan is merely allophonic, though yery [sic, scanned: very] systematic. The most conspicuous case is tone 1 occurring hefore falling tones, …

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Deciding quotation confirmed verbatim in the Hashimoto 1973 text we hold layer at sec. 2.2.3 (printed pp.104-110), with only scanned-level normalizations already noted by the second reader. (2) The source is the standard 612-pp CUP reference grammar of Meixian Hakka, Glottolog's top grammar for the languoid, and it includes instrumental tone traces; classification 'tonal' with no stress rule follows directly from 'The primary supra-segmental features are the six tones' plus the book's complete silence on word stress. (3) downloaded the open JIPA Illustration (Lee & Zee 2009, Meixian speakers recorded 2007): tones + compound tone sandhi, no stress statement -- confirms. with record. sources.quote: 'Citation tone [55] occurs only on checked syllables. Citation tones [...] occur on open syllables and closed syllables with a nasal ending. ... On compounds, before [...], [33] -> [...] and [...] -> [55] ... Citation tones [...] do not undergo tone sandhi before [55] or [33]. ... illustrate simultaneous tone sandhi application to tones on the non-compound-final syllables.' No mention of stress, accent, neutral tone or prominence anywhere in the 5-page article (a full-text search for stress/accent extracted text output: zero hits).
sources.note: Modern instrumental IPA Illustration of the same reference dialect (Meixian); adds a second, independent primary description to a record that rested on one 1973 grammar. downloaded now; confirms tone system with sandhi and silence on word stress.
